name: Grapple Traversal
description: Aim-at-anchor swing and pull traversal, the movement verb that turns a collectible on a spire into a puzzle with a stylish answer. It owns anchor validation — range, line of sight, and the anchor tag so level authors decide what is grappable — the rope constraint while attached, and a release that preserves swing momentum, because the joy of a grapple is energy conservation and a release that clamps velocity feels like hitting glass. Mid-swing steering defers to movement.run_control's air control for the same reason JumpCore defers horizontal velocity: the component that owns horizontal motion applies the multipliers. It grapples geometry only — pulling enemies or items is a combat and inventory verb that would drag targeting rules into a movement component. Ground and air state come from movement.grounded and movement.leftGround so a grapple fired mid-coyote-time behaves exactly like a jump would.

inputs.name: maxRange
inputs.description: Furthest anchor distance. Range is a level-design lever: short ropes make anchor placement a breadcrumb trail, long ropes make the whole skyline reachable.

inputs.name: pullSpeed
inputs.description: Reel-in speed when pulling straight to the anchor. Below jump apex speed the pull feels like a winch; well above it, like a zip.

inputs.name: swingGravityScale
inputs.description: Gravity multiplier while swinging. Reduced gravity lengthens the arc and gives the player time to steer and plan the release.

inputs.name: releaseBoost
inputs.description: Velocity multiplier applied at release. Slightly above 1 so a well-timed release beats a jump — the skill expression of the verb.

inputs.name: anchorTag
inputs.description: Tag marking valid anchors. Authors opt geometry in; nothing is grappable by default.

outputs.name: ropeLength
outputs.description: Current constraint length, exposed so audio and camera can react to swing tension.
